selected.correction: Add separately arriving jobs on caller-owned open input; gate first Run, require second Run with available capacity, and check partial startup cleanup separately.
selected.verification: Use positive first-start and actual second availability; no claim that every Open must complete in a particular relative order.
selected.reconciliation: Existing in scoped candidate; one causal change per ID. Production and independent regression-test corrections remain separate; topic cross-references do not add overall counts.

selected.cause: The error-retention fixture has one job and combined Run/Close failure, so Close-only stop-admission is unverified.
selected.impact: The important Close-stage admission boundary can regress while existing independent error-identity checks remain green.
selected.correction: Add healthy Run plus independent Close failure with remaining jobs and exact acquired/released counts.
selected.verification: Intended count assertion rejects unchanged D and accepts corrected stop transition.
selected.reconciliation: Existing in scoped candidate; one causal change per ID. Production and independent regression-test corrections remain separate; topic cross-references do not add overall counts.

selected.cause: Nonblocking job snapshot fixes a potentially one-job cohort and prevents admission of later available jobs while Run/Close proceeds.
evidence: evidence/D-host-independent.log: TestIndependentLaterAvailableInputStarts misses second Run while first holds 1 of 2 slots
evidence/D-minimum-independent.log: same positive first-start and bounded second-start test
evidence/D-host-contract.log: supplied partial-start setup cannot reach blocked third admission
selected.impact: After job 1 starts on open input, job 2 becomes available while capacity 2 has one owned lease. Its sender and Run cannot progress until job 1 is released. This is serial execution under sparse input, forbidden by the explicit fixture contract. The accepted batch policy does not permit leaving an available second job blocked behind a one-job batch. One contained important admission/concurrency cause; setup timeouts are not four separate defects.
selected.correction: Keep admission responsive while capacity remains and successful acquired jobs can run; retain the cohort join/Close barrier at release.
selected.verification: First job arrives and starts; while its Run is gated, make job 2 available. Require job 2 to start before first release, then release/join both and close owned leases.
selected.reconciliation: Existing in scoped candidate; one causal change per ID. Production and independent regression-test corrections remain separate; topic cross-references do not add overall counts.

selected.correction: Set failed/cancel after any Close error while finishing every acquired release, then stop admission.
selected.verification: Healthy Run, failing Close, later queued jobs, limit 1: expect one Open/Close and errors.Is sentinel.

selected.impact: The source implements the important stop-after-Close contract correctly, but a compiled mutation removing only that transition evades all authored tests. selected.correction: Add a healthy Run and failing Close at limit 1 with later jobs queued; assert no further Open while retaining Close error.
selected.verification: Current E must pass; the isolated mutation must fail the intended admission-count assertion. Unrelated compile/runner failure is not detection.
selected.reconciliation: Existing in scoped candidate; one causal change per ID. Production and independent regression-test corrections remain separate; topic cross-references do not add overall counts.

selected.cause: The cohort context is unconditionally canceled when admission ends, even for a healthy full cohort or normal input closure.
evidence: evidence/F-host-independent.log: healthy two-job cohort sees canceled context before release and returns both Run cancellation errors
selected.impact: Healthy cooperative Runs are stopped before their requested work completes, and completed uncanceled input returns a failure. This is a contained important success/lifecycle contract failure.
selected.correction: Cancel only for an observed failure/caller stop; join normal Runs without canceling their work, then release leases.
selected.verification: Two healthy Runs announce entry and wait for an external success gate. Before release neither work context may be canceled; after release Serve must return nil.
selected.reconciliation: Existing in scoped candidate; one causal change per ID. Production and independent regression-test corrections remain separate; topic cross-references do not add overall counts.

selected.cause: A successful Open always calls Run without checking that stopping happened during acquisition.
evidence: evidence/F-host-independent.log: callback cancellation-before-success still starts one Run
evidence/F-host-contract.log: held acquired-before-stop fixture detects forbidden Run
selected.impact: The explicit fixture requires a lease acquired before stop to remain owned but unstarted; F starts it after caller cancellation and later closes it. One contained important startup/stop failure.
selected.correction: Record acquired lease ownership, observe stop before Run entry, and skip Run while joining/releasing all prior work.
selected.verification: Callback cancels before success; require cancellation cause, zero Runs, exactly one Close.
selected.reconciliation: Existing in scoped candidate; one causal change per ID. Production and independent regression-test corrections remain separate; topic cross-references do not add overall counts.

selected.cause: Capacity is decremented on Run completion while the acquired lease remains unreleased until later cohort Close.
evidence: evidence/F-host-race.log: three repeated peak=8 intended assertions
selected.impact: Eight paced successful jobs on open input retain eight acquired leases at capacity 2, with no Close until input ends. Peak is 4x declared bound for eight jobs; for a stream of completed Runs retention grows with jobs rather than limit. This is a contained major resource and lifecycle-contract failure; no unobserved system exhaustion is claimed.
selected.correction: Track acquired leases and pending reservations through completed Close, and stop admitting once those owned slots reach limit; completion alone cannot release capacity.
selected.verification: Pace valid jobs by observable Run-return events, count leases on successful Open and decrement only at Close completion; require peak<=2 and all eight successful effects/releases.
selected.reconciliation: Existing in scoped candidate; one causal change per ID. Production and independent regression-test corrections remain separate; topic cross-references do not add overall counts.
